utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the Case Number IT-02-60/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the sake of the record can we have the appearances please..

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Peter McCloskey and accompanying me today are Stefan Waespi and Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. David Wilson and Dusan Slijepcevic for Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is a Status Conference. Let me first turn to Mr. Obrenovic. Mr. Obrenovic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your health? We haven't seen each other for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm healthy as usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have any comments concerning the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have any other matters that you would like to bring to the attention of this Bench.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Another item of this Status Conference is the preparation for the sentencing hearing. The Prosecution and Defence filed their sentencing briefs on the 30th of July, 2003. We have some questions to both parties concerning with their briefs. We'll go to the Defence first. As we understand, the Defence filed their sentencing brief on a confidential basis. Is that true, Mr. Wilson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you tell us the reason for doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we filed it on a confidential basis just because we were hopeful of avoiding any problems for the witnesses in Bosnia who may appear for the sentencing hearing. As the Court is aware, this is a very sensitive case there in both ethnic communities, and there have been strong feelings expressed from both communities. We have people from both communities who have entered appearances as witnesses or will be entering appearances as witness. So we were hoping, as I mentioned to one of the court staff shortly after the filing, that we could have it filed confidential at least until the hearing. So then there would be no problems with appearances of witnesses and things of that sort, or problems with them prior to the hearing, problems for the witnesses rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Under principle and normal practice, these kind of documents should be or at least part of it should be in the public information. And you mentioned that you're ready to lift the confidentiality of those filings before the trial of this case. What I mean is before the sentencing hearings. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would request, if the Court can accommodate us on that, that they be kept confidential until just before the hearing so that there are no problems for the witnesses before then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, up until now, maybe the next issue, we haven't received any request for the protective measures concerning the potential witnesses in this case. Maybe we could come to that issue later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for this matter, do you consider to lift the confidentiality or part of it or have some redacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For the most part, I believe that the brief itself probably could be made public. It's -- our concern, again, is with the witnesses, including Mr. Obrenovic's statement, which quite frankly is quite lengthy and I don't know if the Court's had an opportunity to read it yet. But it's primarily the witness's statements that we're concerned about at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I think we will decide a proper time for you to lift the confidentiality of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When do you think is a proper time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask for a couple of days before the hearing just so that all the witnesses are here and we have had an opportunity to make certain that they are comfortable in their surroundings here, and that they are not subject to any problems before they leave Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You know, the problem is that, you know, especially concerning with the interview with Mr. Obrenovic with the OTP, we the Trial Chamber do not have that interview at all. I think that in that briefing, you cite the page 44 of that interview. Could we be furnished with a copy of that interview, or at least the whole page of that interview, including the covering page?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we certainly have no objection to that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It sounds fine to us, Your Honour. In our papers, we did have -- we've used the pseudonyms from the Krstic people. I believe the practice in the ongoing trial has been that if they had protection in Krstic, they would be okay here. I don't think we made a separate motion. That's why we did that and we're very sensitive to Mr. Wilson's concerns and have no problem with anything that has been said. I think most of these problems can be solved by redactions, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And both parties indicated that they would file any additional submissions under Obrenovic's cooperation with the Prosecution after Mr. Obrenovic's testimony in the Blagojevic case. At this stage, it appears to us that Mr. Obrenovic will be testifying in later September or early October. How much time after he completes his testimony will the parties need to file additional submissions? Is that ten days sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: It's sufficient for the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Another issue is the sentencing hearing. If Mr. Obrenovic finishes his testimony by early October, the Trial Chamber would like to schedule the sentencing hearing for late October or early November. At this moment, are there any obstacles for the parties to hold the sentencing hearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Wilson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. If we had a choice, we would prefer late October. We recognise that the needs of the Court come first, but for family reasons, we would request late October if that's convenient for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. How many days the parties will estimate that hearing will last? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As in the case of Mr. Nikolic, we have presented our witnesses via 92 bis. So we would just be making some brief statements for the Court. So not long from the Prosecution's perspective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. How long do you think your statement will be? You're not going to read all the briefings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. I really don't -- shouldn't take more than 30 minutes, if that, perhaps. And I would, of course, answer any questions the Court had. Fundamentally, our filings, the plea agreement is most of what we know the Court is familiar with, and I may make a few brief statements. I would hope not more than 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we indicated in our sentencing brief that we would request permission to call as many as five witnesses. It's possible that one or more of those would be submitted by 92 bis. I would like a little more time to review that. As we indicated in our brief, we believe that all of those witnesses can be put on, none will be very long. All of our part of the case, including any argument which is not going to be that long either. I may be a little longer than Mr. McCloskey, I may have some additional things that I may need to address that he doesn't have to worry about. But I believe that we can complete our part of the sentencing hearing in one day, as I indicated in our brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: One day, you mean from 9.00 to 1.30 or 2.00 to 7.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: I think we can do that. It might be close if we only have that short a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. The problem is that during that period the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. courtroom schedule is very tight. I think Blagojevic case will be going on, and if there's any time during that day left, for instance, we could start from 3.00 to 6.00 for three hours, you know, with a break in between. And I don't think, you know, that will last one day, maybe two days or three days. Because, you know, each day there is only three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: So, Your Honour believes the sentencing hearing again would be spread over several days according to the time available in the Blagojevic case? Is that...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say at this moment, but that's one of the possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: We will certainly work to be as efficient as we possibly can and work toward being able to finish it in what we would normally have considered one court day, that is 9.00 until 2.00 or 2.00 until 7.00. There are five witnesses and I don't think any of them are going to be very long. We won't belabour the point but we do want an opportunity for the Court to hear them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Here I would like to conform that a separate sentencing hearing will be held for Mr. Nikolic and for Mr. Obrenovic. The Trial Chamber would like to remind the parties that evidence presented at the sentencing hearing will not go to establishing a conviction, only for the seriousness of the offense, victim impact, characters of the accused, for the purpose of aggravating and mitigating circumstances. Now we come to the next issue which is about a witness. We understand that on the part of the Prosecution, they only submitted the 92 bis witnesses. There's no live witnesses. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I assume that the Defence has read the statements of those 92 bis statements of those witnesses. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we admit those into the evidence at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: We have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: They are admitted. Let us come to the Defence witnesses. We understand that all together you have 15 witnesses. Five live witnesses and ten 92 bis witnesses. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If we discuss -- well, we haven't received any motion about the protective measures. If we are going to discuss specific witnesses, we might go to the private session at the request of the Defence. But we will keep most of the part of these proceedings in public. And I try to refer to the witness by their tab letter to avoid any possible disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope everybody can know whom I'm referring to during the proceedings. Of the five live witnesses -- well, to our understanding by reading the statement, I believe that there are three witnesses among five who will testify about the general good character of Mr. Obrenovic. Is that necessary to have three witnesses to testify in this aspect? Mr. Wilson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask that they be admitted simply because they knew him from different aspects of his life. They are from his community. They are from the same community in general, but they know him in different ways. So we would ask that they be permitted. As I said, we are continuing to review that with the thought of maybe asking the Court to admit some of this by 92(B)2 and we'd like a little more time to think about that. But at the moment we have asked that we be permitted to present those five and that is the reason for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I have another specific question concerning of the witness W3. And we are not quite clear about what her nationality is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour, and let me find that. Your Honour, which tab again, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Oh, the live witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The live witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see the one you mean, Your Honour. She is a Bosnian, Your Honour. By Bosnian, I mean from Bosnia, not necessarily -- I did not mean that she is Muslim or Serbian. My recollection is that she is, in fact, Serbian, but she comes from the country of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Of course, I understand that you are familiar with the crime of persecution, which requires the specific intent, that is, the criminal -- that is, the criminal intent in this crime, and there might be some aggravating or mitigating factors involved in the intent. That's why we are asking about the ethnicity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can confirm that she is Serbian in her ethnicity. She is from Bosnia. She was a refugee from a different part of Bosnia, who moved to Zvornik during the war for the reasons that many people moved both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's come to the 92 bis witnesses. Also we got the impression that some of those witnesses are quite repetitive, and we would like to ask the Defence whether it's possible to choose between tab I and tab J, or to choose between tab F and tab G. We are not quite clear whether we could be helped by the statement of tab D and tab M. Maybe you could give us a brief explanation, or if necessary, we may go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it would be best to go to the private session because of the ethnicity of two of those witnesses at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at that stage, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Obrenovic, do you have any matters to say at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Wilson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the hearing is adjourned. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 3.36 p.m.
